issues.legal_issue: A death sentence for murder should be commuted to imprisonment for life when the mitigating circumstances, considered together, outweigh the reasons for imposing capital punishment.
material_facts: The appeal concerned death sentences imposed on two murder convicts.

The fatal violence arose amid a longstanding land-possession dispute, and the court considered it probable that the deceased had helped precipitate the tragedy by insisting on retaining or retaking land allotted to the accused.
One appellant was found to have caused only one of the three fatal injuries to a deceased person; the other injuries were attributed to other accused who received lesser sentences.
The appellants were immature youths who appeared to have acted at the instigation of an elder.
The appellants had endured prolonged mental anguish while under sentence of death.
The court considered these circumstances collectively and maintained the convictions while commuting the death sentences.
issues.conclusion: The death sentences were commuted to imprisonment for life on each count, with the sentences to run concurrently.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 302 of the Penal Code, as applied after the 1955 amendment to Section 367(5) of the Code of Criminal Procedure removed the former requirement to give reasons for imposing the lesser penalty, the court had discretion to impose either prescribed penalty. The court stated that death was exacted only where the murder was marked by brutality, and that mitigating circumstances—including a role in provoking the tragedy, the offender’s part in the fatal assault, youth and influence by an elder, and prolonged mental agony under a death sentence—could justify life imprisonment when considered together. It relied on Vivian Rodrick v. State of West Bengal, Gurdip Singh v. State of Punjab, State of Maharashtra v. Naglya Dhavu Kongil, State of Bihar v. Pashupati Singh, Gajanand v. State of U.P., and Ediga Anamma v. State of Andhra Pradesh; it distinguished Brij Bhukhan, Mizaji, and Jagmohan Singh on their facts. The forthcoming 1973 Code’s requirement to give reasons for a death sentence was noted as a legislative trend, not as the basis of decision.

rule.if: capital_sentence_appeal and murder_conviction and land_dispute_helped_precipitate_violence and (appellant_had_limited_role_in_fatal_assault or appellant_was_young_and_influenced_by_elder) and prolonged_mental_agony_under_death_sentence

predicates.capital_sentence_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal in which a death sentence is under review.
predicates.murder_conviction: The person whose sentence is under review was convicted of murder.
predicates.land_dispute_helped_precipitate_violence: A dispute over possession of land helped provoke or precipitate the fatal violence.
predicates.appellant_had_limited_role_in_fatal_assa: The appellant caused only a limited part of the fatal injuries compared with other participants.
predicates.appellant_was_young_and_influenced_by_el: The appellant was an immature or young offender who appeared to have acted under an elder’s instigation.
predicates.prolonged_mental_agony_under_death_sente: The appellant endured prolonged mental anguish while awaiting execution under a death sentence.

issues.definition: When a death sentence for murder is under appeal and the listed circumstances collectively support mitigation, the rule directs that the sentence be commuted to life imprisonment.
